text: Three bears (literally: "big animals") lived in a house: a big one, a middle-sized one, and a little one. One day their porridge was too hot, so they went out to wait. A little girl with yellow hair came along. The door was open, so she went in. She tasted the big bear's porridge: too hot! She tasted the middle bear's: too cold! She tasted the little bear's: just right! And she ate it all up. She sat on the little bear's chair (literally: "sitting thing"), and the chair broke. She was sleepy, so she lay down in the little bear's bed. The three bears came home. The little bear said: "Who ate my porridge?" "Who broke my chair?" Then they found the girl asleep in the little bear's bed! The girl opened her eyes, got scared, ran out, and never came back.

blind.whole: Three big animals, one very big, one middle-sized and one very small, live together in a home. One day their watery food (soup or porridge) is too hot, so they go out to wait. While they are gone, a little girl with gold-coloured hair comes and goes in through the door. She tastes the food: the big animal's is too hot, the middle animal's is too cold, and the small animal's is just right, so she eats all of it. She sits on the small animal's seat (a chair) and it breaks, then she lies down in the small animal's bed and sleeps. The animals come home, and the small animal asks who ate its food and who broke its seat. They find the girl asleep. She wakes up, gets scared, runs out and never comes back.

notes: Translated by hand (2026-10-22) following the translate skill, level: the whole dictionary. kb_memory gave the book's own sentences for this story (lesson none, the appendix), so most sentences adapt one of them, named in each source. Where they differ it is for a closer dictionary word from kb_lookup: mén (door) for kǒu, nǚ-hái-zi (girl) for xiǎo nǚ-rén, tóu-fa (hair) for máo, yǎnjing via bǎ yǎnjing kāi (the form of 睁) for kāi le kàn-de bù-fen, shuǐ duō-de fàn (porridge) for chī-de, zhēn (too) for hěn. Long book sentences were split. Kept: everything in the sketch. Weaker: tasted (ate a little), never (not any more), the bear's "my chair" (this thing), and dà dòng-wù is both the bears and the big bear. Grammar worth the author's attention: (1) bù X yě bù Y has only one reading, doing-as-subject (not-X taken as the subject of also-not-Y); no pattern joins two describing words, so sentences 2 and 13 carry that reading, the same as the book's bù duō bù shǎo. (2) Sentences that end "tǎng zài / zài + xiǎo dòng-wù(-de) shuìjiào-de dì-fang" had no meant reading in the first 500, so the bed gets a sentence of its own (Xiǎo dòng-wù hái yǒu yī-ge shuìjiào-de dì-fang) and is nà-lǐ after. (3) Hòu-lái at the front of a sentence never reads as one word (only hòu + lái) in 500 readings; then is carried by the order. (4) fā-xiàn takes no clause (only zhīdào has a rule for a whole sentence), so found the girl asleep is two sentences. (5) In Zhè-ge dōng-xi jiù huài le the first reading is jiu-only (jiù + a describing word, it is fine); the reading given is jiu-then with huài as a verb. (6) Nǚ-hái-zi xiǎng shuìjiào, jiù / tā jiù tǎng zài nà-lǐ had no want-verb reading in 500, so it is two sentences. (7) Shéi zuò-huài le wǒ-de zhè-ge dōng-xi? does not parse: wǒ-de + zhè-ge is no noun phrase. (8) kb_gloss gives yī-diǎn as one-o'clock, which may trip a blind reader. Glossary proposal: bear -> dà dòng-wù: the test set's own wording; the dictionary's hěn zhòng-de dà dòng-wù is 6 words and a bear comes in almost every sentence. Glossary proposal: lie down in X's bed -> X yǒu yī-ge shuìjiào-de dì-fang, then tǎng zài nà-lǐ: tǎng zài + a long place had no meant reading in 500. Glossary proposal: never came back -> bù huí-lái le: bù … le says not any more; cóng-lái reads only as cóng + lái. Glossary proposal: found X doing Y -> fā-xiàn le X, then a sentence of its own for what X was doing: fā-xiàn takes no clause. Glossary proposal: just right (of heat) -> bù rè yě bù lěng, hěn hǎo: the dictionary's bù duō bù shǎo is about an amount.
